question: Do empirical zero-failure calibration gates and fixed failure penalties improve fresh-seed reliability without hiding fallback costs?
selection: Finite threshold grid -1,0,.025,...,1. Tune cost threshold on calibration only. Select cheapest zero-calibration-failure threshold, ties lowest threshold. Certification is a one-shot accept/reject: any certification failure locks service-all before evaluation. No evaluation-dependent selection.
constraints: Service-all is safe ONLY under this simulator's deterministic known service effect; no general safety guarantee.
No manual-review cost treated as zero. Fallback is executed and charged at one service/entity.
Report every fixed arm, all seeds and failed gates; do not choose a post-evaluation winner.
No ActionOPD, Mamba, biological retention, GEPA or cross-domain superiority claim.
Paired worlds and entities are dependent. Zero-event upper bound uses independent generated pairs conditional on seed and stratified generator, not entities; report seed variability separately.
Zero observed failures does not prove zero risk.
falsifier: Gated policy adds failures on untouched evaluation or does not improve cost/reliability over service-all and exact public history. A rejected certificate is a result, not a reason to retune.
evidence: per-seed costs, failures, unnecessary services, fallback services, prediction metrics, wall-clock and memory scalars
